comments.content: @wannacfuture you wanna pick this one up? You can use the linked pull request as reference.
Maybe it just needs to be reset with a couple reassigns. This seems to be a minor inconvenience but at least it seems consistent with what I've seen on other issues with expired timelines.

Why not check the time stamp of the assignment to the bounty hunter and include that in the last updates calculation? 
I didn't do deep research on this but intuitively it seems to be far more robust to use a time parsing library (by the vercel team) than hard coding a few values. We can't control user input so people might do stuff like `Time: 20 hours` and `Time: 0.83 Days` to mean the same thing. I think we should not hardcode all of these possibilities? 
Or are you suggesting to make a simple formula to multiply the number with a hardcoded duration for the unit of time? We would need to at least support: minutes, hours, days, weeks, and months probably.

Isn't it easier to just use `ms`? Anyways I suppose both give similar results and I haven't done much thinking or research on this matter in a long time. You need to support singular and plural forms as well e.g. `hour` and `hours`

I think its okay, lets standardize times to be measured in smaller resolutions. I think it makes sense to only provide first party support for up to "weeks" because otherwise the partners should break down the tasks into several bounties. Alternatively they can just say `Time: <4 Weeks` etc.
I'm only doing a very cursory review now. 
1. However, the Vercel team (created `ms`) is elite. 
2. The amount of downloads for `ms` is far higher.
Why do you believe that `timestring` is superior?

- Typos should (almost) never happen because labels are reused and the user selects from a list. 
- in my approximately one last year of experience using this system, tasks that are written as longer than a week should be broken down into more tasks. The quality of the experience for both reviewers and bounty hunters drop dramatically with complex tasks that are not provided specific scopes of work / a clear specification. We should discourage use of greater than one week long individual tasks. We use "meta issues" to solve this problem. Basically by making a checklist of up to one week long tasks with clear specifications.

I think a debugging output to display exactly how the comment incentive was calculated is a great idea: e.g. [ Claim 26.5 WXDAI ]
words: 55 @ 0.1 a: 3 @ 5 img: 1 @ 5 h1: 1 @ 1

- Parse `value` directly from the time label. 
  - Include the number, and include the unit (e.g. Hours, Days.)
  - Exclude the `<` symbol.
- Remove the `value` associated in the config. 
- Use `ms` library to derive the value at runtime from the time label based on the number and unit. 
_Originally posted by @pavlovcik in https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquibot/pull/383#discussion_r1240675183_
